claims.statement: The operator-only stuhlmuller Fleet pilot declares rodman@stuhlmuller.net, guards its verified managed non-default domain, and preserves the user's existing password and first-login flag during later UPN reconciliation through ignored password attributes.

The Fleet registration recovery runbook records an approved pilot UPN update rejected by directory uniqueness checks and requires separate review before altering the owner's mail/proxy identity; the pilot rename approval does not authorize owner changes.

On October 7, 2026 UTC, the reviewed Octelium migration applied the original owner oid binding with email fallback disabled, and the guarded mail-only operator plan applied while preserving owner identity and grants. New owner Octelium sessions through Entra callbacks worked before and after mail. The new SMTP address became primary but the old address remained secondary, so address release failed and the pilot rename was not retried. Authenticated exact-owner Exchange Online recipient lookups, including soft-deleted recipients, returned HTTP 404 ManagementObjectNotFoundException; no mail-enabled target was established for Set-MailUser. Microsoft-supported remediation must preserve the existing identity; no Exchange write or additional permission grant occurred. Actual pilot denial and native Mac acceptance remain outstanding.

The operator-only Tailscale provider owns full policy adoption and three distinct-tag reusable, ephemeral, preauthorized CI auth keys with 90-day expiry and explicit committed rotation generations; existing unused federated identities remain protected until final migration retirement.
Tailscale CI plan receives read access and dry-run Application writes guarded by fail-closed admission; the apply tag receives cluster administration.

The fixed CI publisher signs private provider keys on the trusted Mac, requires exactly one new trusted credential authority with matching auth-key metadata and unchanged prior trust mappings, caches that authority's public identity separately from the wrapper's delegated private node-signing key, and requires unique matching metadata for reuse/retirement. It publishes only three fixed secrets without secret argv/output and deletes old client-ID variables only after all writes and metadata checks.

Phase2a removes legacy public DNS restoration paths but retains Cloudflare Tunnel credentials and native Octelium recovery until replacement acceptance; the canonical fixed-inventory mesh DNS helper reuses the scoped cert-manager Cloudflare token.
